structuredContent.description: Read, write, and patch GDScript files; check for parse errors.

tools.name: godot_scripts_read
tools.description:
Read the full text of the script at ``script_path`` (a ``res://`` path,
``.gd`` or ``.cs``).

tools.name: godot_scripts_list
tools.description:
List script files under ``directory`` (recursive, ``res://`` path) for a
backend: ``language="gd"`` (default) lists ``.gd``, ``"cs"`` lists ``.cs``
(C# support: issue #207 Phase 1).

Paginated: ``scripts`` is a window of ``total`` files starting at ``offset``
(default page ``limit`` 200). When ``truncated``, pass ``next_offset`` to page on.

tools.name: godot_scripts_get_for_node
tools.description:
Get the script attached to a node (by scene-relative ``node_path``, or the
selected node when omitted). ``script_path``/``content`` are null if none.

tools.name: godot_scripts_write
tools.description:
Create or overwrite the script at ``script_path`` (``res://``, ``.gd`` or
``.cs``) with ``content``. Reversible via the editor's undo. ``dry_run=True``
writes nothing and reports ``would_overwrite`` so the agent knows whether it is
about to replace an existing script. A real run reports what happened:
``created`` on a fresh file, ``overwrote``/``previous_existed`` when an existing
script was replaced.

C# (``.cs``) writes land the bytes but are NOT usable until a build — the
result carries a ``hint`` saying to validate via a C# build (Phase 2; issue
#207). GDScript is validated via ``get_parse_errors``.

tools.name: godot_scripts_patch
tools.description:
Replace every occurrence of ``find`` with ``replace`` in the script
(``.gd`` or ``.cs``). Errors if ``find`` isn't present. Reversible via undo;
``dry_run`` previews. A ``.cs`` patch still needs a C# build to take effect
(issue #207).

tools.name: godot_scripts_get_parse_errors
tools.description:
Parse-check ``script_path`` and return structured errors (message + line),
or an empty list when it parses cleanly. Use after writing/patching a script.

Scope honesty (#423): this checks GDScript *syntax* — it does NOT catch
class-API misuse (a nonexistent member parses clean and fails at runtime).
For that, run the project: ``godot_runtime_run_and_capture`` reports the
runtime errors (the recommended full-verification pattern); the shader
analogue is ``godot_shader_validate``.

"res://main.tscn"), wait up to ``timeout_seconds``, then return a summary of
``errors`` / ``warnings`` / ``output`` and the exit code. Use this to verify
a change actually runs and to read back failures.

WHEN TO USE: You need to verify a scene runs without an editor open
(CI, automation, smoke test) or you want the full stdout/stderr log.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need to simulate input or inspect live state —
use play_scene() + get_game_scene_tree() / simulate_key() instead.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"scene":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null},"timeout_seconds":{"default":10,"maximum":3600,"minimum":0.1,"type":"number"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_play_scene","description":"Run the game from the editor: play ``scene_path`` (a ``res://*.tscn``) or the
project's main scene when omitted. The game connects to the editor debugger, so
runtime inspection/input tools can reach it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to interact with the running game (simulate input,
inspect live nodes, debug, test assertions).
WHEN NOT TO USE: Headless CI/automation without an editor — use
run_and_capture() instead. That runs Godot in a subprocess and returns
logs without an editor session.

IF THIS FAILS with "scene not found":
  -> The scene_path is wrong. Use get_project_info() to find the main scene,
     or get_scene_tree() to see available scenes.
IF THIS FAILS with "editor not connected":
  -> The Godot editor is not running or the addon is disabled. Check
     get_server_info() for bridge state and follow the troubleshoot prompt.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"scene_path":{"default":"","type":"string"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_stop_scene","description":"Stop the current editor play session.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_is_playing","description":"Report whether a play session is running and which scene.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_get_game_scene_tree","description":"Get the *running* game's live scene tree ({name, type, path, children}).
Requires an active play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload; if the
probe isn't connected, returns ``connected=false`` with a ``hint`` to add it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to inspect node hierarchy, positions, or state while
the game is actively running (e.g., after simulating input to verify movement).
WHEN NOT TO USE: The editor is idle with no play session — use
get_scene_tree() to read the static scene structure instead.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"timeout_ms":{"default":2000,"maximum":600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_capture_game_screenshot","description":"Capture the *running game's* rendered viewport as a PNG image, so you can
visually verify what the player sees — including shader, lighting, and camera
output the editor viewport cannot show (the game is a separate process; the
probe grabs the frame in-process). Read-only. Requires an active play session
with the runtime probe autoload.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game (get_project_info()
     to check), then play_scene again.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"timeout_ms":{"default":2000,"maximum":600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_get_game_output","description":"Read the running game's captured output — ``print()`` lines, script
errors (with the engine's text), and warnings — as a ring of
``{seq, kind, text, time_ms}`` entries (issue #534).

Use it during a play-test to read crash traces and log-based
assertions: the capture keeps working while the game is frozen at a
debugger break (that is exactly when crash traces are readable).
``since_seq`` is an incremental cursor — pass the ``next_seq`` from
your previous call to fetch only newer entries. The ring is bounded
(500); ``dropped`` counts evicted entries honestly, so never assume
the ring holds the whole session.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game, then
     play_scene again.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"since_seq":{"default":0,"type":"integer"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_monitor_property","description":"Start watching ``property`` on the running game's node at ``node_path``
(an absolute path from get_game_scene_tree). The probe captures ``samples``
readings; collect them with get_property_samples. ``on_change_only`` (default)
queues a sample only when the value changed (float ``epsilon``-tolerant, also
inside Vector2/3), so a static property yields fewer deduped entries.

``runtime``: starting the monitor is a side effect on the play session.
Requires a play session + runtime probe; for a single current value use
read_property instead.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"property":{"type":"string"},"samples":{"default":30,"maximum":1000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"},"on_change_only":{"default":true,"type":"boolean"},"epsilon":{"default":0.0001,"type":"number"}},"required":["node_path","property"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_get_property_samples","description":"Return the time series captured by the most recent ``monitor_property``:
``samples`` is ``[{frame, value}]`` (``ready=false`` until the capture completes;
``error`` set if the node/property was invalid).","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_read_property","description":"Read a property from the running game's node at ``node_path`` ONCE and
return its current value (JSON-coerced, same shapes ``monitor_property``
samples use). The dedicated #571 one-shot path: it never touches the
``monitor_property`` capture slot, so an assert or read during a running
capture cannot replace that capture's series. Requires a play session +
runtime probe.

WHEN TO USE: a single current-value check (assertions, "what is X now?").
WHEN NOT TO USE: you want a series over time — use ``monitor_property`` +
``get_property_samples``.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"property":{"type":"string"},"timeout_ms":{"default":2000,"maximum":600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":["node_path","property"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_runtime_find_ui_elements","description":"Locate live UI (Control) nodes in the running game, each with its path, class,
visibility, global ``rect`` (use it with ``simulate_mouse`` to click), and ``text``

``visible_only``. Requires a play session + runtime probe.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"name_contains":{"default":"","type":"string"},"class_filter":{"default":"","type":"string"},"visible_only":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"},"timeout_ms":{"default":2000,"maximum":600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_simulate_key","description":"Send a key event to the running game. ``key`` is a Godot key name
("A", "Space", "Enter", "Escape", …); ``pressed`` false sends a release. Optional
modifier flags (shift/ctrl/alt/meta). Requires a play session + runtime probe.
The injected event carries both keycode and physical_keycode (like real
hardware), so Input Map actions bound either way fire.

WHEN TO USE: You need to send a SINGLE key press or release (e.g., tap
Space to jump, or hold Shift for sprint). Simple, one-off interactions.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need a timed sequence of many inputs — use
play_input_sequence(events=[...], delay_ms=...) instead. That replays a
whole macro with configurable delays between events.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string"},"pressed":{"default":true,"type":"boolean"},"shift":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"},"ctrl":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"},"alt":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"},"meta":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["key"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_simulate_mouse","description":"Send a mouse event at viewport position (``x``, ``y``). With ``button`` empty,
sends motion (with optional ``relative_x``/``relative_y``); with ``button`` =
left/right/middle/wheel_up/wheel_down, sends a button press/release (``pressed``).

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"number"},"y":{"type":"number"},"button":{"default":"","type":"string"},"pressed":{"default":true,"type":"boolean"},"relative_x":{"default":0,"type":"number"},"relative_y":{"default":0,"type":"number"}},"required":["x","y"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_simulate_action","description":"Press or release an input-map action (e.g. "ui_accept", "jump") on the running
game. ``strength`` (0..1) applies to a press. The action must exist in the
project's Input Map.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
IF THIS FAILS with "unknown action":
  → The action is not in the project's Input Map. Add it via
    ProjectSettings → InputMap or use simulate_key() with the raw key name.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"action":{"type":"string"},"pressed":{"default":true,"type":"boolean"},"strength":{"default":1,"type":"number"}},"required":["action"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_play_sequence","description":"Play a sequence of input events in order, ``delay_ms`` apart. Each event is a
dict with ``type`` = "key" | "mouse" | "action" and that type's fields (as for
the simulate_* tools, e.g. ``{"type":"key","key":"Space","pressed":true}``).

WHEN TO USE: You need to replay a recorded or scripted sequence of many
inputs (e.g., a combo move, a login macro, a stress test). Events are
replayed with a fixed delay between each.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You only need a single key press — use simulate_key()
for simplicity. Or you need real-time interactive control — simulate_*
gives per-event control, while this replays a pre-built list.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"events":{"items":{"additionalProperties":true,"type":"object"},"type":"array"},"delay_ms":{"default":0,"maximum":600000,"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}},"required":["events"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_get_stats","description":"Report how many synthesized input events the running game has acknowledged —
use it to confirm injected input is reaching the game.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_record","description":"Start recording the input the running game receives (key + mouse button;
mouse motion only when ``include_motion``). Stop and collect it with
``stop_recording``; the result feeds straight back into ``play_input_sequence``.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"include_motion":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_input_stop_recording","description":"Stop recording and return the captured ``events`` (in the
``play_input_sequence`` format). Polls the addon up to ``timeout_ms`` for the
buffered sequence.

``runtime`` (not read-only): it stops an active recording — a side effect on
the play session (issue #638).","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"timeout_ms":{"default":2000,"maximum":600000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}}]}

tools.name: godot_runtime_run_and_capture
tools.description:
Run the project headless (optionally a specific ``scene`` like
"res://main.tscn"), wait up to ``timeout_seconds``, then return a summary of
``errors`` / ``warnings`` / ``output`` and the exit code. Use this to verify
a change actually runs and to read back failures.

WHEN TO USE: You need to verify a scene runs without an editor open
(CI, automation, smoke test) or you want the full stdout/stderr log.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need to simulate input or inspect live state —
use play_scene() + get_game_scene_tree() / simulate_key() instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_play_scene
tools.description:
Run the game from the editor: play ``scene_path`` (a ``res://*.tscn``) or the
project's main scene when omitted. The game connects to the editor debugger, so
runtime inspection/input tools can reach it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to interact with the running game (simulate input,
inspect live nodes, debug, test assertions).
WHEN NOT TO USE: Headless CI/automation without an editor — use
run_and_capture() instead. That runs Godot in a subprocess and returns
logs without an editor session.

IF THIS FAILS with "scene not found":
  -> The scene_path is wrong. Use get_project_info() to find the main scene,
     or get_scene_tree() to see available scenes.
IF THIS FAILS with "editor not connected":
  -> The Godot editor is not running or the addon is disabled. Check
     get_server_info() for bridge state and follow the troubleshoot prompt.

tools.name: godot_runtime_stop_scene
tools.description: Stop the current editor play session.

tools.name: godot_runtime_is_playing
tools.description: Report whether a play session is running and which scene.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_scene_tree
tools.description:
Get the *running* game's live scene tree ({name, type, path, children}).
Requires an active play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload; if the
probe isn't connected, returns ``connected=false`` with a ``hint`` to add it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to inspect node hierarchy, positions, or state while
the game is actively running (e.g., after simulating input to verify movement).
WHEN NOT TO USE: The editor is idle with no play session — use
get_scene_tree() to read the static scene structure instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_capture_game_screenshot
tools.description:
Capture the *running game's* rendered viewport as a PNG image, so you can
visually verify what the player sees — including shader, lighting, and camera
output the editor viewport cannot show (the game is a separate process; the
probe grabs the frame in-process). Read-only. Requires an active play session
with the runtime probe autoload.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game (get_project_info()
     to check), then play_scene again.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_output
tools.description:
Read the running game's captured output — ``print()`` lines, script
errors (with the engine's text), and warnings — as a ring of
``{seq, kind, text, time_ms}`` entries (issue #534).

Use it during a play-test to read crash traces and log-based
assertions: the capture keeps working while the game is frozen at a
debugger break (that is exactly when crash traces are readable).
``since_seq`` is an incremental cursor — pass the ``next_seq`` from
your previous call to fetch only newer entries. The ring is bounded
(500); ``dropped`` counts evicted entries honestly, so never assume
the ring holds the whole session.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game, then
     play_scene again.

tools.name: godot_runtime_monitor_property
tools.description:
Start watching ``property`` on the running game's node at ``node_path``
(an absolute path from get_game_scene_tree). The probe captures ``samples``
readings; collect them with get_property_samples. ``on_change_only`` (default)
queues a sample only when the value changed (float ``epsilon``-tolerant, also
inside Vector2/3), so a static property yields fewer deduped entries.

``runtime``: starting the monitor is a side effect on the play session.
Requires a play session + runtime probe; for a single current value use
read_property instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_property_samples
godot_runtime_read_property
tools.description:
Read a property from the running game's node at ``node_path`` ONCE and
return its current value (JSON-coerced, same shapes ``monitor_property``
samples use). The dedicated #571 one-shot path: it never touches the
``monitor_property`` capture slot, so an assert or read during a running
capture cannot replace that capture's series. Requires a play session +
runtime probe.

WHEN TO USE: a single current-value check (assertions, "what is X now?").
WHEN NOT TO USE: you want a series over time — use ``monitor_property`` +
``get_property_samples``.

tools.name: godot_runtime_find_ui_elements
tools.description:
Locate live UI (Control) nodes in the running game, each with its path, class,
visibility, global ``rect`` (use it with ``simulate_mouse`` to click), and ``text``
if any. Filter by ``name_contains`` / ``class_filter`` (e.g. "Button") /
``visible_only``. Requires a play session + runtime probe.

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_key
tools.description:
Send a key event to the running game. ``key`` is a Godot key name
("A", "Space", "Enter", "Escape", …); ``pressed`` false sends a release. Optional
modifier flags (shift/ctrl/alt/meta). Requires a play session + runtime probe.
The injected event carries both keycode and physical_keycode (like real
hardware), so Input Map actions bound either way fire.

WHEN TO USE: You need to send a SINGLE key press or release (e.g., tap
Space to jump, or hold Shift for sprint). Simple, one-off interactions.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need a timed sequence of many inputs — use
play_input_sequence(events=[...], delay_ms=...) instead. That replays a
whole macro with configurable delays between events.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_mouse
tools.description:
Send a mouse event at viewport position (``x``, ``y``). With ``button`` empty,
sends motion (with optional ``relative_x``/``relative_y``); with ``button`` =
left/right/middle/wheel_up/wheel_down, sends a button press/release (``pressed``).

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_action
tools.description:
Press or release an input-map action (e.g. "ui_accept", "jump") on the running
game. ``strength`` (0..1) applies to a press. The action must exist in the
project's Input Map.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
IF THIS FAILS with "unknown action":
  → The action is not in the project's Input Map. Add it via
    ProjectSettings → InputMap or use simulate_key() with the raw key name.

tools.name: godot_input_play_sequence
tools.description:
Play a sequence of input events in order, ``delay_ms`` apart. Each event is a
dict with ``type`` = "key" | "mouse" | "action" and that type's fields (as for
the simulate_* tools, e.g. ``{"type":"key","key":"Space","pressed":true}``).

WHEN TO USE: You need to replay a recorded or scripted sequence of many
inputs (e.g., a combo move, a login macro, a stress test). Events are
replayed with a fixed delay between each.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You only need a single key press — use simulate_key()
for simplicity. Or you need real-time interactive control — simulate_*
gives per-event control, while this replays a pre-built list.

tools.name: godot_input_get_stats
tools.description:
Report how many synthesized input events the running game has acknowledged —
use it to confirm injected input is reaching the game.

godot_input_stop_recording
tools.description:
Stop recording and return the captured ``events`` (in the
``play_input_sequence`` format). Polls the addon up to ``timeout_ms`` for the
buffered sequence.

``runtime`` (not read-only): it stops an active recording — a side effect on
the play session (issue #638).

content.text: The air jump fired: the counter went from 1 to 0 mid-air. Now checking that it resets after landing:
Landed on the Ledge (y ≈ 228) with the counter reset to 1. Last check, horizontal movement:

Double jump is in and working: in a live test the player got one extra jump in the air, and it came back after landing. The only file changed is `res://scripts/player.gd`; no scenes or project settings were touched.

## What the controller did before
`res://scripts/player.gd` applied gravity while airborne. `jump` only worked when `is_on_floor()` was true, and `move_left`/`move_right` set the horizontal speed to `SPEED` (220).

## What changed
```gdscript
const MAX_AIR_JUMPS := 1                 # new
var air_jumps_left := MAX_AIR_JUMPS      # new

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if not is_on_floor():
		velocity.y += gravity * delta
	else:
		air_jumps_left = MAX_AIR_JUMPS   # new: refill on landing
	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump"):
		if is_on_floor():
			velocity.y = JUMP_VELOCITY   # same ground jump as before
		elif air_jumps_left > 0:         # new: the one extra jump in the air
			velocity.y = JUMP_VELOCITY
			air_jumps_left -= 1
	# horizontal movement and move_and_slide() unchanged
```
- **Same input:** it uses the existing `jump` action; I didn't add any new inputs.
- **Same air jump strength:** the extra jump uses the same `JUMP_VELOCITY` (-420) as the ground jump.
- **Rest unchanged:** gravity, the ground jump, speed and the order of steps are the same. I also updated the comment at the top of the file, which said there was no double jump yet.

## Checks
1. **Script check:** the script parses cleanly with no errors. This check only covers syntax.
2. **Headless run:** 5 s with no errors or warnings. The timeout is expected because the game has no way to quit.
3. **Live playtest from the editor:**
   - At rest on the Ledge, `air_jumps_left` was 1.
   - A ground jump set velocity.y to -420.
   - Pressing jump again in the air dropped `air_jumps_left` from 1 to 0, so the air jump fired.
   - After landing (y ≈ 228), it was back to 1.
   - Holding `move_right` gave velocity (220, 0), the same speed as before.
   - The game is stopped now.

Two limits on the testing:
- **Third press:** I couldn't capture a full jump arc, because the monitor only records about half a second and injected input arrives late. So I saw the counter hit 0 but didn't directly watch a third press get ignored. The code only allows the air jump when `air_jumps_left > 0`, and the counter can only be refilled by touching the floor.
- **Holding `move_right`:** the player probably walked off the Ledge onto the Floor during that last check. That doesn't affect the result.

**Decision for you:** walking off a ledge without jumping still gives the player one jump in the air. Most platformers do this, and it fits "one extra jump while airborne." If you'd rather the air jump only count after a real ground jump, I can change it so walking off a ledge uses it up.
